messages.content:
Here is our docker-compose.yml:
```yaml
services:
  web:
    image: ghcr.io/acme/web:1.8.2
    ports:
      - "8080:8080"
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgres://app@db:5432/app
      REDIS_URL: redis://cache:6379/0
    depends_on:
      - db
      - cache
    deploy:
      replicas: 2
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "curl", "-f", "http://localhost:8080/health"]
      interval: 30s
      timeout: 5s
      retries: 3
  db:
    image: postgres:16
    volumes:
      - pgdata:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    deploy:
      resources:
        limits:
          memory: 512m
  cache:
    image: redis:7.2-alpine
volumes:
  pgdata:
```
What does the healthcheck do?

The healthcheck runs `curl -f http://localhost:8080/health` inside the web container every 30 seconds. If a request fails or takes longer than 5 seconds, that attempt counts as a failure; after 3 consecutive failures the container is marked unhealthy. Plain `depends_on` does not wait for health; it only orders startup.

Under `web.deploy`:
```yaml
    deploy:
      replicas: 3
```
Everything else is unchanged.
Raise the db memory limit to 1g.

Under `db.deploy.resources.limits`:
```yaml
          memory: 1g
```
The rest of the file is unchanged.
Now change the redis image to redis:7.4-alpine.
